newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic says recalls blood oxygenators.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic says recalls blood oxygenators.

text.p: Medtronic Inc said it started a recall on June 16 of about 4,000 Maxima Forte blood oxygenators due to four reports of possible defects.
Manufacturing of the oxygenators has been temporarily halted until the company determines the cause of the reported defects, said Medtronic spokesman Dick Reid.
The company expects no material impact on revenue or earnings from the recall, he said.
"No patient complications have been reported," he said.
A blood oxygenator takes the place of the lungs during open-heart surgery when the blood is routed through an artificial cardio-pulmonary bypass circuit.
The device contains a bundle of fibers through which the blood passes.

Four Maxima Forte users have reported a slight tinge of blood in the water circulating around the fibers, Reid said. "We tend to think at the moment it's caused by a microscopic hole in the fiber within the heat exchanger," he said.
Medtronic does not make the fiber itself, but buys it from an outside vendor, he said.

Medtronic is the world's largest manufacturer of blood oxygenators. It began selling the Maxima Forte -- its latest generation oxygenator -- in January after it was approved for U.S. marketing by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
